# zugojson

zugojson formats, minifies and validates JSON text. Its parser and
printer are written in [Goose](https://github.com/aardappel/goose), a
memory-safe systems language with no heap, and compiled ahead of time to
C. The package ships that C, so installing it needs no Goose compiler.

The package is a demonstration that Goose can be used to write R
packages. It is not a replacement for jsonlite.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zugojson")
```

zugojson builds on Linux and macOS. Windows is not supported yet.

## Usage

``` r

library(zugojson)

cat(json_format('{"a": [1, 2.50, {"b": null}], "s": "x"}'))
#> {
#>   "a": [
#>     1,
#>     2.5,
#>     {
#>       "b": null
#>     }
#>   ],
#>   "s": "x"
#> }

json_minify('{ "a" : [ 1, 2 ] }')
#> [1] "{\"a\":[1,2]}"

json_valid(c("[1, 2]", "[1, 2", NA))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA
```

A syntax error is a condition of class `zugojson_parse_error`. Its
`byte` field holds the offset where parsing stopped.

``` r

tryCatch(json_format("[1, 2"), zugojson_parse_error = function(e) e$byte)
#> [1] 5
```

## How it works

The JSON code is in `tools/goose/zugojson.goose`. `tools/regenerate.sh`
compiles it with a pinned Goose compiler into `src/zugojson_goose.c`, a
C file with no `main`.

The parsed document lives in one contiguous block. Each node links to
its next sibling with a 4-byte offset relative to itself, so the tree
holds no pointers.

Generated Goose code needs a runtime. The stock runtime ends the process
on any error, writes to stdout and stderr, and installs process-wide
signal handlers. That is unacceptable inside R, so zugojson replaces it
with `src/goose_r_runtime.c`:

- A Goose runtime error, such as a failed bounds check, becomes an R
  error of class `zugojson_runtime_error`, and later calls keep working.
- Goose’s guard-page fault handler is installed only while Goose code
  runs. R’s own handlers are restored afterwards.
- Nothing writes to stdout or stderr, and nothing can end the R process.

## Performance

On a 14.7 MB document, zugojson took about twice as long as jsonlite
2.0.0 for each task. That is the median of seven runs, with R 4.6.1 on
Linux.

| Task         | zugojson | jsonlite |
|--------------|----------|----------|
| Minify       | 0.43 s   | 0.18 s   |
| Pretty-print | 0.48 s   | 0.29 s   |
| Validate     | 0.20 s   | 0.11 s   |

# Package index

## All functions

- [`json_format()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugojson/reference/json_format.md)
  : Format JSON text
- [`json_minify()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugojson/reference/json_minify.md)
  : Minify JSON text
- [`json_valid()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugojson/reference/json_valid.md)
  : Test whether strings are valid JSON
